items.description: The boundary module (app/routes/) contains no import of the database session object, keeping the layering contract: persistence access is confined to the repository layer
The service module (app/services/) contains no ORM import (no SQLAlchemy Session, Query, or model class import), satisfying the ORM-only contract for the service layer

The boundary module (app/routes/) contains no ORM import (no SQLAlchemy Session, Query, or model class import), satisfying the ORM-only contract for the boundary layer independently of the session-import check
The application resolves the database connection string exclusively from the DATABASE_URL environment variable; no literal connection string appears anywhere in the source tree
Every stock endpoint in the boundary returns a JSON response body; no endpoint returns server-rendered HTML
Rendering <App> in MemoryRouter at '/stock/file' mounts the StockForm page without redirecting away
Rendering <App> in MemoryRouter at '/stock/:sku/:location' mounts the StockRecord page without redirecting away

When a warehouse team member POSTs a SKU, location, quantity, and inventory_code to the stock API, a 2xx response is returned and the stock record is retrievable from the database with the exact filed values
When a previously filed stock record is fetched by SKU and location from the API, the response body contains the quantity exactly as originally submitted
When a previously filed stock record is fetched by SKU and location from the API, the response body contains the combined inventory_code exactly as originally submitted
When the API receives a second stock filing for the same SKU and location pair, the response is successful and only one record exists for that pair in the database
When the API receives a second stock filing for the same SKU and location pair with different values, the retrieved record reflects the updated quantity rather than the original quantity
The StockForm root element carries its design-guide data-testid (e.g. data-testid='stock-form') rather than an inline style
Filling SKU, location, quantity, and inventory_code then submitting the form dispatches a POST to the stock API boundary
When the API returns a validation error that names the offending field, the form renders that field-level message adjacent to the named field
The StockRecord root element carries its design-guide data-testid (e.g. data-testid='stock-record') rather than an inline style
When the API returns a stock record, the retrieval view displays the quantity value exactly as returned
When the API returns a stock record, the retrieval view displays the combined inventory_code exactly as returned
Submitting the stock form a second time for the same SKU and location pair surfaces no error state in the UI

Filing a second stock record for an already-stored per-run-unique (sku, location) pair collapses to the existing row — the table contains exactly one row for that pair and no uniqueness error is surfaced to the caller
An attempt to persist a stock_records row with a null value for quantity, sku, location, or inventory_code is rejected by the real branch database with an integrity error (not a mock)
An attempt to persist a stock_records row with quantity < 0 is rejected by the real branch database CHECK constraint ck_stock_records_quantity_non_negative (not a mock)

Two writes for the same per-run-unique (sku, location) key each execute inside a single transaction; the resulting table contains exactly one row for that pair (delta count scoped to the test's own rows = 1), confirming the upsert is atomic

The service layer raises a domain error before any DB round-trip when a file-stock call supplies a negative quantity, so rejection occurs at the service layer guard and not only at the DB CHECK constraint

The service layer raises a domain error before any DB round-trip when a pick would overdraw the current stock level for the given (sku, location), so the overcommit rejection occurs at the service layer guard
When a file-stock request omits or supplies an invalid value for a field, the boundary validation error response body names that specific field rather than returning a generic error message
When an existing stock record is updated via the upsert path, the created_at column retains its original value and is not overwritten, confirming audit-timestamp immutability on in-place update

The Alembic migration for stock_records completes a single downgrade then upgrade cycle without error, marked @pytest.mark.migration and run against the real branch database; the downgrade target is never 'base'

Rows seeded with a per-run-unique key before the migration upgrade are present with their original column values after the upgrade completes, confirming the additive migration preserves pre-existing records
